content.intro: Learn group_concat in the context of aggregate functions and grouping. This lesson covers the supplied syllabus topic, demonstrates a representative MySQL example, and finishes with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Analytical queries define a row grain, compute metrics at that grain, and make ordering and tie behavior explicit. Aggregate queries collapse rows into groups; window functions calculate across related rows without collapsing the current row set.

content_blocks.title: Apply the idea
content_blocks.text: Calculate a small result by hand, run the grouped/windowed query, and check row grain, ties, and NULL behavior. Write down the expected result before running the snippet. Compare actual output with the reference, then try one normal case and one edge case.

content_blocks.code: SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(item ORDER BY item SEPARATOR ', ') AS items FROM (SELECT 'books' AS category, 'Atlas' AS item UNION ALL SELECT 'books', 'Novel' UNION ALL SELECT 'pens', 'Gel') AS inventory GROUP BY category;
content_blocks.expected_output: One row per category contains an ordered, comma-separated item list.
